objects.definition: typedef voidpf (*alloc_func) OF((voidpf opaque, uInt items, uInt size));
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom memory allocation callbacks used by zlib. It allocates a block for items * size bytes using an application-provided allocator with an opaque context.

objects.definition: typedef void   (*free_func)  OF((voidpf opaque, voidpf address));
objects.description: Function pointer type for custom memory free callbacks used by zlib, paired with alloc_func and receiving the same opaque context.
Incomplete forward declaration of zlib’s internal stream state structure. Applications must not access its contents; it is managed internally by zlib.

objects.definition:
typedef struct z_stream_s {
    z_const Bytef *next_in;     /* next input byte */
    uInt     avail_in;  /* number of bytes available at next_in */
    uLong    total_in;  /* total number of input bytes read so far */

    Bytef    *next_out; /* next output byte will go here */
    uInt     avail_out; /* remaining free space at next_out */
    uLong    total_out; /* total number of bytes output so far */

    z_const char *msg;  /* last error message, NULL if no error */
    struct internal_state FAR *state; /* not visible by applications */

    alloc_func zalloc;  /* used to allocate the internal state */
    free_func  zfree;   /* used to free the internal state */
    voidpf     opaque;  /* private data object passed to zalloc and zfree */

    int     data_type;  /* best guess about the data type: binary or text
                           for deflate, or the decoding state for inflate */
    uLong   adler;      /* Adler-32 or CRC-32 value of the uncompressed data */
    uLong   reserved;   /* reserved for future use */
} z_stream;

typedef z_stream FAR *z_streamp;
objects.description: Primary stream state structure passed to deflate/inflate APIs. Holds input/output buffers, counters, error message, internal state pointer, application-provided alloc/free callbacks with opaque, and checksum/state fields. Applications must initialize zalloc, zfree, and opaque before init calls, and then use through zlib APIs.

objects.definition:
typedef struct gz_header_s {
    int     text;       /* true if compressed data believed to be text */
    uLong   time;       /* modification time */
    int     xflags;     /* extra flags (not used when writing a gzip file) */
    int     os;         /* operating system */
    Bytef   *extra;     /* pointer to extra field or Z_NULL if none */
    uInt    extra_len;  /* extra field length (valid if extra != Z_NULL) */
    uInt    extra_max;  /* space at extra (only when reading header) */
    Bytef   *name;      /* pointer to zero-terminated file name or Z_NULL */
    uInt    name_max;   /* space at name (only when reading header) */
    Bytef   *comment;   /* pointer to zero-terminated comment or Z_NULL */
    uInt    comm_max;   /* space at comment (only when reading header) */
    int     hcrc;       /* true if there was or will be a header crc */
    int     done;       /* true when done reading gzip header (not used
                           when writing a gzip file) */
} gz_header;

typedef gz_header FAR *gz_headerp;
objects.description: Structure describing gzip header metadata exchanged with deflateSetHeader() and inflateGetHeader(), including extra fields, file name, comment, OS, and flags.

objects.definition:
typedef unsigned (*in_func) OF((void FAR *,
                                z_const unsigned char FAR * FAR *));
objects.description: Callback type used by inflateBack() to supply input. Returns number of input bytes provided and outputs a pointer to that data via second argument. First argument is user descriptor.

objects.definition: typedef int (*out_func) OF((void FAR *, unsigned char FAR *, unsigned));
objects.description: Callback type used by inflateBack() to consume output. Writes len bytes from provided buffer, returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure. First argument is user descriptor.

objects.definition: typedef struct gzFile_s *gzFile;    /* semi-opaque gzip file descriptor */
objects.description: Opaque handle type for gzip file operations (gzopen/gzread/gzwrite/etc.). Points to an internal structure managed by zlib; applications treat gzFile as an abstract handle.
Abbreviated, exposed subset of the internal gz file state used solely to implement the gzgetc() macro efficiently. Users should not modify these fields directly.

functions.name: zlibVersion
functions.description: Returns the runtime version string of the zlib library. Typically used to check ABI compatibility with the headers used at compile time (compare against ZLIB_VERSION).
requirements: No arguments.
Callers may compare the first character of the returned string with ZLIB_VERSION to verify compatibility.

functions.name: deflate
functions.description: Compresses input data from strm->next_in into strm->next_out, updating the stream state. Can be called repeatedly; respects flush behavior (Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH, Z_BLOCK, Z_FULL_FLUSH, Z_FINISH).
requirements: strm must have been successfully initialized by deflateInit(), deflateInit2(), or deflateReset().
Before each call, ensure either strm->avail_in > 0 or strm->avail_out > 0 so that at least one action is possible; strm->avail_out should never be zero on entry.
flush must be one of: Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH, Z_BLOCK, Z_FULL_FLUSH, or Z_FINISH.
If deflate returns Z_OK with strm->avail_out == 0, call again with more output space to retrieve remaining pending output.
When using Z_SYNC_FLUSH or Z_FULL_FLUSH, ensure strm->avail_out > 6 to avoid repeated flush markers due to zero space on return.
For one-shot compression using Z_FINISH in the first call, allocate output of at least deflateBound().
Do not call with NULL next_in/next_out; doing so causes Z_STREAM_ERROR.

functions.name: deflateEnd
functions.description: Frees all dynamically allocated state for a deflate stream. Discards unprocessed input and does not flush pending output.
requirements: strm must be a valid stream previously initialized for deflation.
After deflateEnd(), the stream may not be used unless re-initialized.

functions.name: inflate
functions.description: Decompresses data from strm->next_in to strm->next_out, updating the stream state. Supports optional early-return controls via flush (Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_BLOCK, Z_TREES, Z_FINISH).
requirements: strm must have been successfully initialized by inflateInit(), inflateInit2(), or inflateReset().
Before each call, ensure that at least one of: strm->avail_in > 0 or strm->avail_out > 0, otherwise no progress may be made.
flush must be one of: Z_NO_FLUSH, Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_BLOCK, Z_TREES, or Z_FINISH.
If inflate returns Z_OK with strm->avail_out == 0, call again with more output space to retrieve more output.
For one-shot decompression with Z_FINISH, strm->avail_out must be large enough for the entire uncompressed data; otherwise a window will be allocated and more calls may be made.
When Z_NEED_DICT is returned, use inflateSetDictionary() with the indicated Adler-32 to continue.
If decoding gzip/zlib was enabled via inflateInit2(), header type may be auto-detected as configured.
Do not call with NULL next_in/next_out; doing so causes Z_STREAM_ERROR.

functions.name: inflateEnd
functions.description: Frees all dynamically allocated state for an inflate stream. Discards unprocessed input and does not flush pending output.
requirements: strm must be a valid stream previously initialized for inflation.
After inflateEnd(), the stream may not be used unless re-initialized.

functions.name: deflateSetDictionary
functions.signature: int deflateSetDictionary(z_streamp strm, const Bytef *dictionary, uInt dictLength)
functions.description: Sets a preset compression dictionary for deflate without producing output. Must match the dictionary used by the decompressor.
requirements: strm must be initialized for deflate and in a valid state.
dictionary must not be NULL; dictLength is the length of the provided dictionary.
For zlib-wrapped streams: call immediately after deflateInit/deflateInit2/deflateReset and before any deflate() calls.

For raw deflate: call either before any deflate() call, or immediately after a block boundary when all input has been consumed and all output delivered with Z_BLOCK/Z_PARTIAL_FLUSH/Z_SYNC_FLUSH/Z_FULL_FLUSH.
Dictionary effectiveness may be limited by window size; only up to (window size - 262) bytes may be effectively used.
On return, strm->adler is set to the Adler-32 of the dictionary for zlib/gzip; not set for raw deflate.

functions.name: deflateGetDictionary
functions.description: Retrieves the current sliding dictionary maintained by deflate. Optionally copies it into the provided buffer and/or returns its length.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
If dictionary is non-NULL, it must have enough space; 32768 bytes is always sufficient.
If dictionary is NULL, only the length is returned; if dictLength is NULL, it is not set.

functions.name: deflateCopy
functions.description: Creates a complete duplicate of the source deflate stream state into dest. Useful for branching compression strategies.
requirements: source must be a valid, initialized deflate stream.
dest must be a valid z_stream structure pointer; zalloc in source must not be NULL.
Be aware the copy can be large and costly in memory and time; free copies with deflateEnd().

functions.name: deflateReset
functions.description: Resets a deflate stream as if deflateEnd() followed by deflateInit() had been called, but reuses the existing internal state allocation. Leaves compression level and attributes unchanged.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream (zalloc and state non-NULL).

functions.name: deflateParams
functions.signature: int deflateParams(z_streamp strm, int level, int strategy)
functions.description: Dynamically changes the deflate compression level and strategy. May emit a Z_BLOCK to finalize input so far.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
level and strategy must be valid per deflateInit2() semantics.

If deflateParams() internally performs deflate(Z_BLOCK) and there is insufficient output space, the parameter change will not take effect and Z_BUF_ERROR is returned; caller may retry with more output space.
To ensure parameters change on first try, flush outstanding output (e.g., call deflate(Z_BLOCK) until strm->avail_out != 0) and provide no new input before calling deflateParams().

functions.name: deflateTune
functions.signature: int deflateTune(z_streamp strm, int good_length, int max_lazy, int nice_length, int max_chain)
functions.description: Fine-tunes low-level match search parameters of the deflate algorithm for expert optimization. Intended only for advanced use.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream initialized by deflateInit()/deflateInit2().
Parameters influence internal algorithm behavior; caller should understand deflate.c internals to use meaningfully.

functions.name: deflateBound
functions.description: Returns an upper bound on the compressed size of sourceLen bytes for the current deflate stream configuration. Useful to pre-allocate output for single-pass compression.
requirements: strm must be initialized by deflateInit()/deflateInit2().
Call after deflateSetHeader() if used, to include header overhead in the bound.

functions.name: deflatePending
functions.description: Reports how many full bytes and remaining bits of pending output are buffered but not yet made available in strm->next_out/avail_out.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.
If pending is non-NULL, it is set to the number of pending bytes.
If bits is non-NULL, it is set to a value in [0,7] for pending bits.

functions.name: deflatePrime
functions.signature: int deflatePrime(z_streamp strm, int bits, int value)
functions.description: Inserts up to 16 bits into the deflate output stream before any compressed data. Intended for appending to previous raw deflate streams.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream configured for raw deflate (no zlib/gzip wrapper).
Must be called before the first deflate() after deflateInit2() or deflateReset().
bits must be <= 16; the least significant 'bits' of 'value' will be inserted.
May return Z_BUF_ERROR if internal buffer lacks room.

functions.name: deflateSetHeader
functions.description: Sets metadata for a gzip header to be written when deflating with a gzip wrapper (requested via deflateInit2()).
requirements: strm must be a deflate stream initialized with deflateInit2() for gzip or reset accordingly.
Call after deflateInit2()/deflateReset() and before the first deflate().
If head->name or head->comment are not Z_NULL, they must be zero-terminated strings.
If head->extra is not Z_NULL, head->extra_len bytes must be available.
If head->hcrc is non-zero, a header CRC will be included.
xflags is ignored (set from compression level).

functions.name: inflateSetDictionary
functions.signature: int inflateSetDictionary(z_streamp strm, const Bytef *dictionary, uInt dictLength)
functions.description: Provides a preset dictionary to the inflater. Must be called immediately after inflate() returns Z_NEED_DICT. For raw inflate, may be called at any time to set/augment the window.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
dictionary must not be NULL; dictLength provides its length.
If called after Z_NEED_DICT, the dictionary must match the Adler-32 indicated by strm->adler from the last inflate() call.
For raw inflate, if provided dictionary is smaller than the window and the window already has data, the dictionary amends existing window data.

functions.name: inflateGetDictionary
functions.description: Retrieves the current sliding dictionary maintained by inflate. Optionally copies it into the provided buffer and/or returns its length.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
If dictionary is non-NULL, it must have enough space; 32768 bytes is always sufficient.
If dictionary is NULL, only the length is returned; if dictLength is NULL, it is not set.

functions.name: inflateSync
functions.description: Skips invalid compressed data until a possible full-flush point (00 00 FF FF) is found, or input is exhausted. Produces no output. Used to recover from data errors.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream with input provided in next_in/avail_in.
Call repeatedly with more input until Z_OK (found point), Z_DATA_ERROR (no point), or end of data. Z_BUF_ERROR indicates no more input was provided.

functions.name: inflateCopy
functions.description: Creates a complete duplicate of the source inflate stream state into dest. Useful for random access or checkpointing during decompression.
requirements: source must be a valid, initialized inflate stream.
dest must be a valid z_stream pointer; zalloc in source must not be NULL.
Free copies with inflateEnd().

functions.name: inflateReset
functions.description: Resets an inflate stream as if inflateEnd() followed by inflateInit() had been called, but reuses existing internal allocations. Keeps attributes set by inflateInit2().
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream (zalloc and state non-NULL).

functions.name: inflateReset2
functions.description: Like inflateReset(), but allows changing the wrap/window configuration (as in inflateInit2()). Frees and reallocates window storage as needed.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
windowBits must be valid per inflateInit2() semantics; invalid values cause Z_STREAM_ERROR.

functions.name: inflatePrime
functions.signature: int inflatePrime(z_streamp strm, int bits, int value)
functions.description: Inserts up to 16 bits into the inflate input bit buffer before consuming bytes from next_in. Used to align to a bit boundary or resume within a byte when doing raw inflate.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream configured for raw inflate (no wrappers).
Must be called before the first inflate() after inflateInit2() or inflateReset().
bits must be <= 16; the least significant 'bits' of 'value' are inserted.
If bits is negative, the input bit buffer is emptied first; can then be called again to insert bits.

functions.name: inflateMark
functions.description: Returns a packed value describing inflate's current position within a block: lower 16 bits = bytes already emitted for the current code or bytes to copy in stored block; upper bits = number of bits back in input of the current code, or -1 for special states.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
Interpretation: upper=-1, lower=0 means between blocks; upper=-1, lower>0 means in a stored block with that many bytes remaining to copy.

functions.name: inflateGetHeader
functions.description: Requests that gzip header information be stored into the provided gz_header structure during inflate. head->done indicates completion.
requirements: strm must be initialized by inflateInit2() or reset by inflateReset().
Call before the first inflate() call on the gzip stream.
If extra is not Z_NULL, head->extra_max must specify max to write; after completion, extra_len and extra are set (possibly truncated).
If name/comment are not Z_NULL, up to name_max/comm_max bytes (zero-terminated unless truncated) are written.
Absent fields set to Z_NULL to indicate absence.
When decoding a zlib stream, head->done is set to -1 (no gzip header).

functions.name: inflateBack
functions.signature: int inflateBack(z_streamp strm, in_func in, void *in_desc, out_func out, void *out_desc)
functions.description: Performs a raw inflate using callback functions for input and output, potentially avoiding window-to-output copies by using the provided window as the output buffer.
requirements: Call inflateBackInit() first to allocate state and set the window; provide the same strm to inflateBack().
strm->next_in and strm->avail_in may optionally provide initial input before callbacks; otherwise in() will be called immediately.
in must be a function of type in_func that returns a byte count and sets a buffer pointer; it must return 0 to indicate no input available.
out must be a function of type out_func that writes provided data and returns 0 on success or non-zero on failure.
Neither in() nor out() may modify the output window supplied to inflateBackInit().
On return, strm->next_in/avail_in reflect unused input from the last in() call.

functions.name: inflateBackEnd
functions.description: Frees all memory allocated by inflateBackInit() for use with inflateBack().
requirements: strm must be a stream previously initialized with inflateBackInit().

functions.name: zlibCompileFlags
functions.description: Returns a bitmask describing compile-time options and sizes used to build the zlib library (type sizes, options, features).
requirements: No arguments; interpret bits per documentation comments in zlib.h.

functions.name: compress
functions.signature: int compress(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong sourceLen)
functions.description: Convenience function to compress a buffer using default compression level. On entry, *destLen is the destination buffer size; on return, it is set to the actual compressed size.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer of at least compressBound(sourceLen) bytes; on entry, *destLen must hold that buffer size.
destLen must not be NULL; source must not be NULL.
sourceLen is the size of source in bytes.

functions.name: compress2
functions.signature: int compress2(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong sourceLen, int level)
functions.description: Compresses a buffer with the specified compression level, as in deflateInit. On return, *destLen is set to the compressed size.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer of at least compressBound(sourceLen) bytes; on entry, *destLen must hold that buffer size.
destLen must not be NULL; source must not be NULL.
level must be Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION or in the range [0,9].

functions.name: compressBound
functions.description: Returns an upper bound on the compressed size of sourceLen bytes when using compress()/compress2().
requirements: sourceLen is the length of data to be compressed.

functions.name: uncompress
functions.signature: int uncompress(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong sourceLen)
functions.description: Decompresses a buffer into the destination buffer. On entry, *destLen is the total size of destination. On return, *destLen is the actual uncompressed size.
requirements: dest must point to a buffer large enough to hold the entire uncompressed data; on entry, *destLen is the size of dest.
source and dest must not be NULL.
sourceLen is the size of source in bytes.
The uncompressed size must be known externally or destination sized conservatively; if too small, returns Z_BUF_ERROR and fills what it can.

functions.name: uncompress2
functions.signature: int uncompress2(Bytef *dest, uLongf *destLen, const Bytef *source, uLong *sourceLen)
functions.description: Like uncompress(), but consumes exactly *sourceLen bytes from source and updates *sourceLen to the number of bytes actually consumed.
requirements: dest must point to a sufficiently large buffer; on entry, *destLen is its size.
source must not be NULL; sourceLen must not be NULL and points to available input length; on return, updated to bytes consumed.

functions.name: gzdopen
functions.description: Associates a gzFile stream with an existing file descriptor for reading (decompressing) or writing (compressing) with gzip format semantics.
requirements: fd must be a valid file descriptor (not -1); gzdopen does not verify validity until I/O occurs.
mode must specify 'r', 'w', or 'a' (no '+'); may include level (e.g., "wb9") and strategy flags ('f','h','R','F'), 'T' for transparent write, and possibly 'e' for close-on-exec where supported.
If you want to keep the original descriptor open, dup() it before calling gzdopen, since gzclose() will close the descriptor associated with the gzFile.

functions.name: gzbuffer
functions.description: Sets the internal I/O buffer size for a gzFile. Must be called after open and before any other read/write calls. Affects gzprintf() maximum output.
requirements: file must be a valid gzFile from gzopen()/gzdopen().
Call before any other I/O on file; otherwise returns -1.
size is the desired buffer size in bytes.

functions.name: gzsetparams
functions.signature: int gzsetparams(gzFile file, int level, int strategy)
functions.description: Dynamically changes compression level and strategy for a gzFile opened for writing; flushes pending data before applying changes.
requirements: file must be opened for writing via gzopen()/gzdopen().
level and strategy must be valid as per deflateInit2() semantics.

functions.name: gzread
functions.signature: int gzread(gzFile file, voidp buf, unsigned len)
functions.description: Reads and decompresses up to len uncompressed bytes into buf. Transparently detects non-gzip input and reads directly in that case. Continues across concatenated gzip members; trailing non-gzip data after gzip streams is ignored.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
buf must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
len must fit into an int; if too large to fit in int, nothing is read and Z_STREAM_ERROR is set.
For concurrently written files, if end-of-input reached, check gzerror() for Z_OK or Z_BUF_ERROR, and use gzclearerr() to reset EOF if retrying later.

functions.name: gzfread
functions.signature: z_size_t gzfread(voidp buf, z_size_t size, z_size_t nitems, gzFile file)
functions.description: Reads and decompresses up to nitems of size bytes into buf, fread()-like wrapper around gzread().
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
If size*nitems overflows z_size_t, nothing is read, returns 0, and sets Z_STREAM_ERROR.
If EOF is hit and only a partial item remains (uncompressed length not multiple of size), the partial final item is read and EOF set; length not reported.

functions.name: gzwrite
functions.signature: int gzwrite(gzFile file, voidpc buf, unsigned len)
functions.description: Compresses and writes len bytes from buf to the gzFile.
requirements: file must be opened for writing or appending.
buf must point to at least len bytes.
Returns number of uncompressed bytes written or 0 on error.

functions.name: gzfwrite
functions.signature: z_size_t gzfwrite(voidpc buf, z_size_t size, z_size_t nitems, gzFile file)
functions.description: Compresses and writes nitems of size bytes, fwrite()-like wrapper around gzwrite().
requirements: file must be opened for writing or appending.
If size*nitems overflows z_size_t, nothing is written, returns 0, and sets Z_STREAM_ERROR.

functions.name: gzprintf
functions.description: Formats, compresses, and writes data to a gzFile, like fprintf. Returns number of uncompressed bytes written or a negative zlib error code.
requirements: file must be opened for writing or appending.

The uncompressed output per call is limited to 8191 bytes or one less than the size set by gzbuffer(); exceeding this limit causes an error (0) with nothing written, and may overflow if zlib was compiled without safe snprintf().
format must be a valid printf-style format string; variadic arguments must match the format.

functions.name: gzputs
functions.description: Compresses and writes the null-terminated string s (without the terminator) to a gzFile.
requirements: file must be opened for writing or appending.
s must be a valid null-terminated string.

functions.name: gzgets
functions.description: Reads up to len-1 decompressed bytes or up to and including a newline into buf, and null-terminates if any bytes were read.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
buf must point to a buffer of at least len bytes.
If len < 1, buf is left untouched and NULL is returned.

functions.name: gzputc
functions.description: Compresses and writes a single byte (c converted to unsigned char) to a gzFile.
requirements: file must be opened for writing or appending.

functions.name: gzgetc
functions.description: Reads and decompresses one byte from a gzFile. Implemented as a macro for speed; falls back to the function when needed.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
As a macro, does not perform all safety checks (e.g., file != NULL).

functions.name: gzungetc
functions.description: Pushes back one character to be returned by the next read on file.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
c must not be -1; pushing may fail if a character is already pushed and not yet read, except immediately after open where at least one buffer’s worth is allowed.
Pushed character is discarded if stream is repositioned with gzseek()/gzrewind().

functions.name: gzflush
functions.description: Flushes pending output to file. When flush is Z_FINISH, completes the current gzip stream; further writes start a new gzip member.
requirements: file must be opened for writing.
flush must be a valid deflate flush value (e.g., Z_SYNC_FLUSH, Z_FINISH, etc.).
Frequent flushing degrades compression.

functions.name: gzrewind
functions.description: Rewinds a gzFile opened for reading to the start of the uncompressed stream.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.

functions.name: gzeof
functions.description: Returns 1 if the end-of-file indicator is set for reading, 0 otherwise. EOF is set only after a read attempts to go past end of input.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.
To continue reading a concurrently written file after EOF, use gzclearerr() if gzerror() indicates Z_OK or Z_BUF_ERROR.

functions.name: gzdirect
functions.description: Returns 1 if reading is a direct copy (input not a gzip stream), 0 if reading a gzip stream with decompression. When writing, returns 1 if transparent writing ("wT") was requested.
requirements: Calling immediately after gzopen()/gzdopen() may allocate buffers to probe the file; call gzbuffer() first if you need to set the buffer size.
When writing, transparent mode must have been requested; otherwise returns 0.

functions.name: gzclose
functions.description: Closes a gzFile, flushing pending output if necessary, and deallocates state. After closing, gzerror() cannot be called on that file.
requirements: file must be a valid gzFile; must not call more than once on the same file.
On success returns Z_OK; various zlib or errno-based errors otherwise.

functions.name: gzclose_r
functions.description: Closes a gzFile that is only used for reading, avoiding linking compression code when statically linking.
requirements: file must be a gzFile opened for reading.
Do not use for writing/appending.

functions.name: gzclose_w
functions.description: Closes a gzFile that is only used for writing/appending, avoiding linking decompression code when statically linking.
requirements: file must be a gzFile opened for writing/appending.
Do not use for reading.

functions.name: gzerror
functions.description: Returns a string describing the last error on file, and sets *errnum to the zlib error code (Z_ERRNO for system errors, check errno).
requirements: file must be a valid gzFile.
errnum may be NULL if the numeric code is not needed.
Returned string is owned by the library and may be invalidated by subsequent calls or by closing the file.

functions.name: gzclearerr
functions.description: Clears the error and EOF indicators on a gzFile, allowing further operations (e.g., to continue reading a concurrently written file).
requirements: file must be a valid gzFile.

functions.name: adler32
functions.signature: uLong adler32(uLong adler, const Bytef *buf, uInt len)
functions.description: Computes or updates an Adler-32 checksum over buf[0..len-1]. If buf is Z_NULL, returns the initial value for a new checksum.
requirements: Provide previous checksum in adler (use 0L with buf==Z_NULL, len==0 to get initial).
buf may be NULL only when requesting the initial value.
len is the number of bytes to process.

functions.name: adler32_z
functions.signature: uLong adler32_z(uLong adler, const Bytef *buf, z_size_t len)
functions.description: Same as adler32(), but len is a size_t-compatible type (z_size_t).
requirements: Same as adler32(), but len may be larger as per z_size_t.

functions.name: crc32
functions.signature: uLong crc32(uLong crc, const Bytef *buf, uInt len)
functions.description: Computes or updates a CRC-32 over buf[0..len-1] with standard pre/post conditioning. If buf is Z_NULL, returns the initial value for a new CRC.
requirements: Provide previous CRC in crc (use 0L with buf==Z_NULL, len==0 to get initial).
buf may be NULL only when requesting the initial value.
len is the number of bytes to process.

functions.name: crc32_z
functions.signature: uLong crc32_z(uLong crc, const Bytef *buf, z_size_t len)
functions.description: Same as crc32(), but len is a size_t-compatible type (z_size_t).
requirements: Same as crc32(), but len may be larger as per z_size_t.

functions.name: crc32_combine_op
functions.signature: uLong crc32_combine_op(uLong crc1, uLong crc2, uLong op)
functions.description: Combines two CRC-32 checksums as if over concatenated data, using a precomputed operator op from crc32_combine_gen(). Faster when op is reused.
requirements: op must be generated from a length using crc32_combine_gen() (or crc32_combine_gen64() as appropriate).
crc1 and crc2 are CRC-32 values of the two sequences.

functions.name: deflateInit_
functions.signature: int deflateInit_(z_streamp strm, int level, const char *version, int stream_size)
functions.description: Internal versioned initializer for deflate. Use via deflateInit macro, which passes ZLIB_VERSION and sizeof(z_stream).
requirements: strm->zalloc, strm->zfree, and strm->opaque must be set (or NULL to use defaults) before calling.
level must be Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION or in [0,9].
version should be ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size must be sizeof(z_stream).

functions.name: inflateInit_
functions.signature: int inflateInit_(z_streamp strm, const char *version, int stream_size)
functions.description: Internal versioned initializer for inflate. Use via inflateInit macro, which passes ZLIB_VERSION and sizeof(z_stream).
requirements: strm->next_in, avail_in, zalloc, zfree, and opaque should be set appropriately before calling; zalloc/zfree may be NULL to use defaults.
version should be ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size must be sizeof(z_stream).

functions.name: deflateInit2_
functions.signature: int deflateInit2_(z_streamp strm, int level, int method, int windowBits, int memLevel, int strategy, const char *version, int stream_size)
functions.description: Internal versioned initializer for deflate with extra parameters. Use via deflateInit2 macro.
requirements: strm->zalloc, zfree, opaque must be set (or NULL for defaults).
method must be Z_DEFLATED.
windowBits typically 8..15 (with extensions: negative for raw, +16 for gzip). 8 maps to 9 in current deflate() implementation.
memLevel in [1,9].
strategy one of Z_DEFAULT_STRATEGY, Z_FILTERED, Z_HUFFMAN_ONLY, Z_RLE, Z_FIXED.
version should be ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size must be sizeof(z_stream).

functions.name: inflateInit2_
functions.signature: int inflateInit2_(z_streamp strm, int windowBits, const char *version, int stream_size)
functions.description: Internal versioned initializer for inflate with wrap/window configuration. Use via inflateInit2 macro.
requirements: strm->zalloc, zfree, opaque must be set (or NULL for defaults).
windowBits 8..15 (0 to use header's window), negative for raw, +32 for auto gzip/zlib, +16 for gzip only.
windowBits must be >= the compressor's windowBits, or 15 if unknown.
version should be ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size must be sizeof(z_stream).

functions.name: inflateBackInit_
functions.signature: int inflateBackInit_(z_streamp strm, int windowBits, unsigned char *window, const char *version, int stream_size)
functions.description: Internal versioned initializer for inflateBack(). Allocates and initializes state using a caller-supplied output window buffer.
requirements: strm->zalloc, zfree, opaque must be set (or NULL for defaults).
windowBits in 8..15; for general deflate streams use 15 and supply a 32K window.
window must point to a buffer of size 1<<windowBits.
version should be ZLIB_VERSION; stream_size must be sizeof(z_stream).

functions.name: gzgetc_
functions.description: Function form of gzgetc for backward compatibility. Reads and returns one decompressed byte, or -1 on EOF/error.
requirements: file must be opened for reading.

functions.name: gzopen
functions.description: Opens a path for gzip-compressed reading or writing with zlib's gz* API. Supports compression level and strategy in mode, transparent writing ('T'), appending ('a'), exclusive create ('x'), and close-on-exec ('e' where supported).
requirements: path and mode must be valid C strings.
mode must include exactly one of 'r','w','a'; '+' is not allowed.
On append, gzopen does not validate existing file contents; it simply appends a new gzip member.

functions.name: gzseek
functions.signature: z_off_t gzseek(gzFile file, z_off_t offset, int whence)
functions.description: Sets the file position for the next gzread/gzwrite relative to whence in terms of uncompressed bytes. SEEK_END is not supported.
requirements: file must be open; supports reading (emulated and possibly slow) and writing (only forward seeks by writing zeros).
When writing, seeking backward is an error.

functions.name: gztell
functions.description: Returns the current position for next gzread/gzwrite, measured in uncompressed bytes from the start of the stream.
requirements: file must be a valid gzFile.

functions.name: gzoffset
functions.description: Returns the current compressed file offset (actual file position). Excludes yet-unconsumed buffered input when reading. Includes any prefix bytes before the gzip stream.
requirements: file must be a valid gzFile.
Returns -1 on error.

functions.name: adler32_combine
functions.signature: uLong adler32_combine(uLong adler1, uLong adler2, z_off_t len2)
functions.description: Combines two Adler-32 checksums into one as if over concatenated data of lengths len1 and len2 (only len2 is needed).
requirements: len2 is signed; negative values yield meaningless results (do not use negative).
adler1/adler2 are checksums of the first and second data segments respectively.

functions.name: crc32_combine
functions.signature: uLong crc32_combine(uLong crc1, uLong crc2, z_off_t len2)
functions.description: Combines two CRC-32 checksums into one as if over concatenated data, using len2 of the second segment.
requirements: len2 is the length of the second segment; negative values are not meaningful.
crc1/crc2 are CRC-32 values of the first and second data segments.

functions.name: crc32_combine_gen
functions.description: Generates an operator value corresponding to len2 for use with crc32_combine_op() to combine CRCs efficiently multiple times.
requirements: len2 must be the length of the second segment.

functions.name: zError
functions.description: Returns a constant string description for a given zlib error code.
requirements: err is a zlib error code (e.g., Z_OK, Z_STREAM_ERROR, etc.).
Returned pointer is to a static string; do not modify or free.

functions.name: inflateSyncPoint
functions.description: Reports whether inflate is at a synchronization point (a location where inflateSync() could resynchronize).
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.

functions.name: get_crc_table
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal CRC-32 table used by zlib.
requirements: The returned table pointer is to read-only data; do not modify.

functions.name: inflateUndermine
functions.description: Undocumented testing/debug aid to enable or disable validations in inflate. Not for general use.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
Behavior is internal/undocumented; use only in controlled test contexts.

functions.name: inflateValidate
functions.description: Enables or disables validation of checks (e.g., checksum) while inflating. Undocumented helper.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.
check controls validation; exact semantics are internal.

functions.name: inflateCodesUsed
functions.description: Returns the number of codes used by the inflate tables in the stream. Useful for diagnostics/analysis.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.

functions.name: inflateResetKeep
functions.description: Resets inflate state while preserving the allocated window and possibly other settings. Internal/undocumented variant.
requirements: strm must be a valid inflate stream.

functions.name: deflateResetKeep
functions.description: Resets deflate state while preserving the allocated internal state. Internal/undocumented variant.
requirements: strm must be a valid deflate stream.

functions.name: gzvprintf
functions.signature: int gzvprintf(gzFile file, const char *format, va_list va)
functions.description: va_list variant of gzprintf(): formats, compresses, and writes to a gzFile. Returns number of uncompressed bytes written or a negative zlib error code.
requirements: file must be opened for writing or appending.
format and va must be valid for vprintf-style formatting.
Subject to the same output size limits as gzprintf(), which depend on gzbuffer().

data_types.description: A byte buffer with no required structure or encoding. May contain any values (0x00–0xFF) and any length, including empty. Used as raw bytes for operations like dictionaries, checksums, or generic input/output buffers.

A sequence of bytes representing text terminated by a NUL (0x00) byte. May contain any bytes except the terminator for the main content. Used where C-style strings are expected (e.g., filename, comment fields).

A byte stream that may be a raw DEFLATE block stream, a zlib-wrapped DEFLATE stream, or a gzip-wrapped DEFLATE stream. May include valid compressed data, concatenated members (for gzip), or malformed sequences for robustness testing.

generators.generator:
import os
import random
import struct
import zlib
from typing import List

# This generator targets "arbitrary binary data" used by zlib fuzz stubs as FUZZ_PARAM_STR inputs.
# We aim to produce valid and interesting buffers that exercise:
# - deflateSetDictionary/inflateSetDictionary: realistic dictionaries (ASCII text, repeated patterns, binaries)
# - deflate/inflateSync: compressed-like prefixes, flush markers, raw/gzip/zlib headers
# - checksum functions: varied sizes and byte distributions
# The output is a single bytes buffer; the fuzzer will split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# Therefore we pack multiple segments back-to-back and include varied cases; consumers will slice.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Prebuilt interesting chunks
PLAIN_TEXTS = [
    b"\n".join([
        b"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
        b"Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow!",
        b"Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs.",
    ]),
    (b"A" * 1024) + (b"B" * 1024) + (b"A" * 1024),
    b"Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. " * 20,
]

# Simple raw deflate block (stored block) creator for small data to look like valid input for inflateSync scans
# Stored block format: 3-bit BFINAL/BTYPE=00 in bitstream; for simplicity, we craft a zlib-wrapped minimal with zlib header
# but also include the 00 00 FF FF pattern that inflateSync searches for.
FLUSH_MARKER = b"\x00\x00\xff\xff"

def make_zlib_stream(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # zlib wrapper (CMF/FLG) + deflate-compressed payload; use Python's zlib
    return zlib.compress(payload, level=6)


def make_gzip_stream(payload: bytes, mtime: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # Build a simple gzip member with default header using zlib module
    c = zlib.compressobj(level=6, wbits=16 + 15)
    comp = c.compress(payload) + c.flush()
    return comp


def make_raw_deflate(payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # raw deflate stream (no zlib/gzip wrapper)
    c = zlib.compressobj(level=6, wbits=-15)
    return c.compress(payload) + c.flush()


def random_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-./\n\t"
    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def random_binary(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return rng.randbytes(n) if hasattr(rng, 'randbytes') else os.urandom(n)


def build_dictionary_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pool: List[bytes] = []
    # Mix of small and large dicts; up to 32K effective window
    sizes = [0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 32, 64, 128, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 32768]
    for _ in range(6):
        n = rng.choice(sizes)
        if n == 0:
            pool.append(b"")
            continue
        kind = rng.randrange(5)
        if kind == 0:
            pool.append(random_ascii(rng, n))
        elif kind == 1:
            # repetitive patterns
            base = random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(1, min(64, n)))
            pool.append((base * (n // len(base) + 1))[:n])
        elif kind == 2:
            pool.append(random_binary(rng, n))
        elif kind == 3:
            # sliding English-like text
            text = rng.choice(PLAIN_TEXTS)
            if len(text) >= n:
                pool.append(text[:n])
            else:
                pool.append((text * (n // len(text) + 1))[:n])
        else:
            # bytes 0..255 cycle
            seq = bytes([i % 256 for i in range(n)])
            pool.append(seq)
    return pool


def build_gz_header_fields(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build plausible fields for name/comment/extra used by deflateSetHeader callers.
    # We'll emit zero-terminated strings and an extra field with subfields.
    # Format here is just concatenated name\0 comment\0 extra_len(2) extra
    name = random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 40))
    comment = random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
    extra = bytearray()
    # a couple of subfields: ID1 ID2 LEN data
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 2)):
        sid = bytes([rng.randrange(0,256), rng.randrange(0,256)])
        data = random_binary(rng, rng.randint(0, 32))
        extra += sid + struct.pack('<H', len(data)) + data
    blob = name + b"\x00" + comment + b"\x00" + struct.pack('<H', len(extra)) + bytes(extra)
    return blob


def build_inflate_sync_bytes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct a buffer with random data, with occasional valid flush markers and gzip/zlib members
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    while total < 800:
        choice = rng.randrange(6)
        if choice == 0:
            # raw data
            chunk = random_binary(rng, rng.randint(1, 64))
        elif choice == 1:
            # add a flush marker
            chunk = FLUSH_MARKER
        elif choice == 2:
            # small zlib member
            payload = random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
            chunk = make_zlib_stream(payload)
        elif choice == 3:
            # small gzip member
            payload = random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
            chunk = make_gzip_stream(payload)
        elif choice == 4:
            # raw deflate piece
            payload = random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
            chunk = make_raw_deflate(payload)
        else:
            # repeated 00 to emulate stored block headers inside deflate streams
            chunk = b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 32)
        parts.append(chunk)
        total += len(chunk)
        if total > 800:
            break
    return b"".join(parts)


def assemble_segments(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    segments: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Dictionaries pool samples
    for d in build_dictionary_pool(rng):
        segments.append(d)

    # 2) Plain text and patterned data for general FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    segments.append(rng.choice(PLAIN_TEXTS))
    segments.append(random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 256)))
    segments.append((b"0123456789" * 50)[:377])

    # 3) Compressed-looking data for inflate/deflate variations
    src_small = random_ascii(rng, rng.randint(0, 256))
    segments.append(make_zlib_stream(src_small))
    segments.append(make_gzip_stream(src_small))
    segments.append(make_raw_deflate(src_small))

    # 4) Inflate sync friendly data containing markers
    segments.append(build_inflate_sync_bytes(rng))

    # 5) Gzip header-related blob content
    segments.append(build_gz_header_fields(rng))

    # 6) Edge cases: empty, single byte, long repeated
    segments.append(b"")
    segments.append(bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256)]))
    segments.append(b"Z" * 2048)

    # 7) Binary with all byte values
    segments.append(bytes(range(256)))

    # Concatenate while respecting size limit
    out = bytearray()
    for seg in segments:
        if len(out) + len(seg) > MAX_TOTAL:
            # try to truncate the last piece if helpful
            remain = MAX_TOTAL - len(out)
            if remain <= 0:
                break
            out.extend(seg[:remain])
            break
        out.extend(seg)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return assemble_segments(rng)
